# Unreleased

Staging note for the next release. Fold it into that release's `<tag>.md` (the release job reads `.github/release-notes/<tag>.md`) and delete this file.

## New

- **Drag files, folders, images and text into the chat input.** A workspace file dropped from the VS Code Explorer or an editor tab becomes an `@` file chip (read when you send, as if picked from the `@` list); a folder becomes an `@` folder chip, which is a search scope rather than the folder's whole contents. Images go through the image attachment (only for models that read images; at most 10 per message, 5 MB each), dropped text loses hidden characters, and a link is added as text without being fetched. Files that look like they hold secrets (`.env` files, keys and certificates, `.ssh` and cloud credential folders), files outside the workspace, and files from the operating system's file manager other than images are refused, and the input says which file and why; a refused file is never read. In VS Code, hold Shift while dragging. VS Code 1.140 and later stop Explorer and tab drops from reaching extension webviews (microsoft/vscode#339036); until VS Code fixes that, use `@` for workspace files. JetBrains IDEs are reported not to deliver drops to the chat (its browser is off-screen); use `@` there.

- **See what fills the context window.** Beside the session cost under the prompt, a context meter shows the share of the model's window in use ("Context 43%"), in the theme's warning colour from 60 percent and its error colour from 80 percent or once the oldest messages are being left out. Click it, press Enter on it, or rest the pointer on it to see what the context holds: a bar and a table of the system prompt, tool definitions, rules, attached files, your messages, replies, tool calls, tool results, terminal output, images, reasoning, free space and the room kept for the reply, with the largest items by name ("Read src/app.ts: 12k") and the prompt cache state. The split is estimated and scaled to the provider's token count. Compact now and New session are in the same panel. It replaces the small battery that appeared from 60 percent with these actions in a hover tooltip. Nothing about what is sent to the model changes.

- **Choose what to keep in the context.** Beside Compact now in the context panel, "Choose what to keep…" opens a dialog that lists the conversation's tool results, terminal output, attached files, images and older turns, by category and largest first, each with its size and a checkbox, and a running total of the context after the change ("After: 41k tokens (21%)"). Before you apply, it says what the edit costs the prompt cache: the next request re-reads everything from the first changed message on ("re-reads 77k tokens at full price (about $0.27 more)"), or nothing extra when the cache is cold. A removed tool result is sent as a one-line note in the same tool message ("[output removed by you: 12k tokens, Read src/app.ts]"), so every tool call keeps its result; attached files and images become one line each; older turns are removed whole and only from the start of the conversation, and the latest turn is always kept. Nothing is deleted from the session: until you send the next message, Undo in the context panel puts everything back at no cost, and later the dialog can put a removed item back as a new edit. Nothing changes unless you apply the dialog; compaction and pruning work as before.
